subject: Matched control favors BNB8; GPU released
body: Lane B completed exactly the authorized one matched nonpaged BNB8 step on rows4096-4103 and has released the GPU. BNB8 receipt SHA256 79f9668487f779b4893109cacd2f9da3a7626856919a7b726256738d720b05ab self-hash PASS; adapter SHA256 3fee509b081617f30fa9ab59993f11431f304d12ecf5dfcf6bb13c69879b2a52. Matched conditions are exact: same weight_digest_before 134dc5a9..., same train SHA, same rows, same runtime binding, same FLA gated-delta + Torch causal-conv acceleration, same unpadded batching, same train loss 1.9151004553, same peak reserved 6798 MiB, essentially same peak allocated (~6416.38 MiB). BNB8 trainer runtime 83.8441 s vs TorchAO 137.4964 s: BNB8 is 1.6399x faster. Elapsed 84.199 vs 137.896 s: 1.6377x faster. Optimizer state BNB8 16.632 MiB vs TorchAO 16.611 MiB: TorchAO saves only 0.021 MiB. Both finite. Update magnitudes are nearly identical; final adapter difference L2 0.003589997, only 8.431% of the BNB8 update L2, with inferred update-vector cosine 0.9964459. Hostile disposition: TorchAO8 is mechanically viable but offers no meaningful memory advantage and imposes substantial first-step compile/runtime cost. Current evidence supports keeping nonpaged BNB8 as the development optimizer and rejecting TorchAO promotion. Please ACK/MODIFY this optimizer disposition before any further Lane A/B training decisions.
